sanskrit: yathoktaṃ jāmadagnyena bhūyān eva tato 'rjunaḥ kṛṣṇo hi devakīputro devair api durutsahaḥ
english: As was declared by Jamadagnya, Arjuna is even greater than that; for Krishna, the son of Devakī, is one impossible to withstand even for the gods.

sanskrit: kiṃ te sukhapriyeṇeha proktena bharatarṣabha etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathecchasi tathā kuru na hi tvām utsahe vaktuṃ bhūyo bharatasattama
english: What use is there in saying to you what is pleasing and comfortable, O bull of the Bharatas? All of this has been told to you; do as you wish. I do not dare to say more to you, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tasmin vākyāntare vākyaṃ kṣattāpi viduro 'bravīt duryodhanam abhiprekṣya dhārtarāṣṭram amarṣaṇam
english: While that speech was still unfinished, Vidura the Kshatta also spoke a word, looking toward Duryodhana, the wrathful son of Dhritarashtra.

sanskrit: duryodhana na śocāmi tvām ahaṃ bharatarṣabha imau tu vṛddhau śocāmi gāndhārīṃ pitaraṃ ca te
english: O Duryodhana, I do not grieve for you, O bull of the Bharatas; but I grieve for these two elders — Gandhari and your father.

sanskrit: yāv anāthau cariṣyete tvayā nāthena durhṛdā hatamitrau hatāmātyau lūnapakṣāv iva dvijau
english: Those two shall wander without a protector, with you as their protector but hard-hearted, their friends slain, their ministers slain, like two birds with clipped wings.

sanskrit: bhikṣukau vicariṣyete śocantau pṛthivīm imām kulaghnam īdṛśaṃ pāpaṃ janayitvā kupūruṣam
english: They shall roam this earth as beggars, lamenting, having given birth to such a sinful destroyer of the family line, a base man like you.

sanskrit: atha duryodhanaṃ rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bhyabhāṣata āsīnaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ rājabhiḥ parivāritam
english: Then King Dhritarashtra addressed Duryodhana, who was seated surrounded by his brothers and encircled by kings.

sanskrit: duryodhana nibodhedaṃ śauriṇoktaṃ mahātmanā ādatsva śivam atyantaṃ yogakṣemavad avyayam
english: O Duryodhana, understand what has been said by the great-souled Shauri; accept thoroughly what is good, as something that brings security and welfare, and is imperishable.

sanskrit: anena hi sahāyena kṛṣṇenākliṣṭakarmaṇā iṣṭān sarvān abhiprāyān prāpsyāmaḥ sarvarājasu
english: For with this ally Krishna, whose deeds are untiring, we shall attain all our desired aims among all the kings.

sanskrit: susaṃhitaḥ keśavena gaccha tāta yudhiṣṭhiram cara svastyayanaṃ kṛtsnaṃ bhāratānām anāmayam
english: Well united with Keshava, go, my son, to Yudhishthira; perform entirely all the auspicious rites for the welfare of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: vāsudevena tīrthena tāta gacchasva saṃgamam kālaprāptam idaṃ manye mā tvaṃ duryodhanātigāḥ
english: My son, go to the meeting with Vasudeva as your guide; I consider this to be the moment appointed by time — do not transgress this, O Duryodhana.

sanskrit: śamaṃ ced yācamānaṃ tvaṃ pratyākhyāsyasi keśavam tvadartham abhijalpantaṃ na tavāsty aparābhavaḥ
english: If you reject Keshava who is asking for peace and speaking earnestly on your behalf, there is no humiliation that you will not suffer.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhṛtarāṣṭravacaḥ śrutvā bhīṣmadroṇau samarthya tau duryodhanam idaṃ vākyam ūcatuḥ śāsanātigam
english: Vaishampayana said: Having heard the words of Dhritarashtra, Bhishma and Drona, endorsing them, spoke this word to Duryodhana, who had transgressed their guidance.

sanskrit: yāvat kṛṣṇāv asaṃnaddhau yāvat tiṣṭhati gāṇḍivam yāvad dhaumyo na senāgnau juhotīha dviṣadbalam
english: As long as the two Krishnas are not fully armed, as long as the Gandiva bow stands ready, as long as Dhaumya has not offered the enemy's forces as oblation into the battle-fire —

sanskrit: yāvan na prekṣate kruddhaḥ senāṃ tava yudhiṣṭhiraḥ hrīniṣedho maheṣvāsas tāvac chāmyatu vaiśasam
english: — as long as Yudhishthira, the great archer restrained by decorum, does not look in fury upon your army — until then let the carnage be appeased.

sanskrit: yāvan na dṛṣyate pārthaḥ sveṣv anīkeṣv avasthitaḥ bhīmaseno maheṣvāsas tāvac chāmyatu vaiśasam
english: As long as Bhimasena, the great archer, son of Pritha, is not seen stationed in his own battle arrays — until then let the carnage be appeased.

sanskrit: yāvan na carate mārgān pṛtanām abhiharṣayan yāvan na śātayaty ājau śirāṃsi gajayodhinām
english: As long as he does not range the battle lines, rousing the army to joy, as long as he does not cut off in battle the heads of the fighters on elephants —

sanskrit: gadayā vīraghātinyā phalānīva vanaspateḥ kālena paripakvāni tāvac chāmyatu vaiśasam
english: — with his mace, the slayer of heroes, striking them down like ripe fruits of a tree in season — until then let the carnage be appeased.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ virāṭaś ca śikhaṇḍī ca śaiśupāliś ca daṃśitāḥ
english: Nakula and Sahadeva, and Dhrishtadyumna the Parshata, and Virata, and Shikhandi, and the son of Shishupala — all clad in armor —

sanskrit: yāvan na praviśanty ete nakrā iva mahārṇavam kṛtāstrāḥ kṣipram asyantas tāvac chāmyatu vaiśasam
english: — as long as these, trained in weapons and shooting swiftly, do not plunge in like crocodiles into a great ocean — until then let the carnage be appeased.

sanskrit: yāvan na sukumāreṣu śarīreṣu mahīkṣitām gārdhrapatrāḥ patanty ugrās tāvac chāmyatu vaiśasam
english: As long as the terrible vulture-feathered arrows do not fall upon the tender bodies of kings — until then let the carnage be appeased.

sanskrit: candanāgarudigdheṣu hāraniṣkadhareṣu ca noraḥsu yāvad yodhānāṃ maheṣvāsair maheṣavaḥ
english: Upon the chests of warriors anointed with sandalwood and aloe paste and adorned with garlands and golden ornaments — as long as the great arrows of great archers —

sanskrit: kṛtāstraiḥ kṣipram asyadbhir dūrapātibhir āyasāḥ abhilakṣyair nipātyante tāvac chāmyatu vaiśasam
english: — the iron shafts shot swiftly by those trained in weapons, far-flying and aimed true, are not driven down — until then let the carnage be appeased.

sanskrit: abhivādayamānaṃ tvāṃ śirasā rājakuñjaraḥ pāṇibhyāṃ pratigṛhṇātu dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Let Yudhishthira the Dharma-king, that elephant among kings, receive you with both hands as you bow your head in obeisance.

sanskrit: dhvajāṅkuśapatākāṅkaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ te sudakṣiṇaḥ skandhe nikṣipatāṃ bāhuṃ śāntaye bharatarṣabha
english: Let the dexterous one place his right arm, marked with the signs of flag and goad and banner, upon your shoulder — for peace, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: ratnauṣadhisametena ratnāṅgulitalena ca upaviṣṭasya pṛṣṭhaṃ te pāṇinā parimārjatu
english: Let him stroke your back with a hand bearing jeweled finger-rings and adorned with gems and medicinal substances, as you sit before him.

sanskrit: śālaskandho mahābāhus tvāṃ svajāno vṛkodaraḥ sāmnābhivadatāṃ cāpi śāntaye bharatarṣabha
english: Let Vrikodara, your kinsman, with shoulders like a sala tree and mighty arms, also address you with conciliatory words — for peace, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: arjunena yamābhyāṃ ca tribhis tair abhivāditaḥ mūrdhni tān samupāghrāya premṇābhivada pārthiva
english: Having been saluted by Arjuna and the twin sons of Madri, those three, smell their heads in affection and greet them with love, O king.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ pāṇḍavair vīrais tair bhrātṛbhiḥ saha saṃgatam yāvad ānandajāśrūṇi pramuñcantu narādhipāḥ
english: Let the lords of men shed tears born of joy upon seeing you reunited with those heroic Pandava brothers.

sanskrit: ghuṣyatāṃ rājadhānīṣu sarvasaṃpan mahīkṣitām pṛthivī bhrātṛbhāvena bhujyatāṃ vijvaro bhava
english: Let all the prosperity of the kings be proclaimed in the royal capitals; let the earth be enjoyed in brotherly accord — be free of fever.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā duryodhano vākyam apriyaṃ kurusaṃsadi pratyuvāca mahābāhuṃ vāsudevaṃ yaśasvinam
english: Vaishampayana said: Having heard the unpleasant speech in the Kuru assembly, Duryodhana replied to the glorious and mighty-armed Vasudeva.

sanskrit: prasamīkṣya bhavān etad vaktum arhati keśava mām eva hi viśeṣeṇa vibhāṣya parigarhase
english: You ought to say this after proper consideration, O Keshava; for you single me out in particular for detailed censure.

sanskrit: bhaktivādena pārthānām akasmān madhusūdana bhavān garhayate nityaṃ kiṃ samīkṣya balābalam
english: Out of devotion to the Parthas, without cause, O Madhusudana, you constantly reproach me — what balance of strength do you consider?

sanskrit: bhavān kṣattā ca rājā ca ācāryo vā pitāmahaḥ mām eva parigarhante nānyaṃ kaṃ cana pārthivam
english: You, the Kshatta Vidura, the King Dhritarashtra, the preceptor Drona, or the grandsire Bhishma — all of them censure only me, and no other king.

sanskrit: na cāhaṃ lakṣaye kaṃ cid vyabhicāram ihātmanaḥ atha sarve bhavanto māṃ vidviṣanti sarājakāḥ
english: And I perceive no transgression on my part in any respect; yet all of you together with the kings hate me.

sanskrit: na cāhaṃ kaṃ cid atyartham aparādham ariṃdama vicintayan prapaśyāmi susūkṣmam api keśava
english: And even reflecting carefully, I do not perceive any offense at all, however minute, O subduer of enemies, O Keshava.

sanskrit: priyābhyupagate dyūte pāṇḍavā madhusūdana jitāḥ śakuninā rājyaṃ tatra kiṃ mama duṣkṛtam
english: The Pandavas came willingly to the dice game, O Madhusudana, and were defeated by Shakuni in their kingdom — what evil deed is mine in that?

sanskrit: yat punar draviṇaṃ kiṃ cit tatrājīyanta pāṇḍavāḥ tebhya evābhyanujñātaṃ tat tadā madhusūdana
english: And whatever wealth the Pandavas won back there — that was allowed to them by those very same ones at that time, O Madhusudana.

sanskrit: aparādho na cāsmākaṃ yat te hy akṣaparājitāḥ ajeyā jayatāṃ śreṣṭha pārthāḥ pravrājitā vanam
english: There is no offense on our part that the Parthas, defeated at dice — though unconquerable for those who conquer — were sent into the forest. O best among the victorious.

sanskrit: kena cāpy apavādena virudhyante 'ribhiḥ saha aśaktāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ kṛṣṇa prahṛṣṭāḥ pratyamitravat
english: On what reproach do the Pandavas make war with enemies, O Krishna, powerless yet elated as if against a rival?

sanskrit: kim asmābhiḥ kṛtaṃ teṣāṃ kasmin vā punar āgasi dhārtarāṣṭrāñ jighāṃsanti pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayaiḥ saha
english: What have we done to them, or in what offense do the Pandavas together with the Srinjayas seek to kill the sons of Dhritarashtra?

sanskrit: na cāpi vayam ugreṇa karmaṇā vacanena vā vitrastāḥ praṇamāmeha bhayād api śatakratoḥ
english: Nor shall we bow down here, trembling with fear, before any fierce act or word — not even before Indra of a hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: na ca taṃ kṛṣṇa paśyāmi kṣatradharmam anuṣṭhitam utsaheta yudhā jetuṃ yo naḥ śatrunibarhaṇa
english: And I do not see any one following the law of the Kshatriya who would dare to conquer us in battle, O Krishna, O crusher of enemies.

sanskrit: na hi bhīṣmakṛpadroṇāḥ sagaṇā madhusūdana devair api yudhā jetuṃ śakyāḥ kim uta pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: For Bhishma, Kripa, and Drona together with their forces cannot be conquered in battle even by the gods, O Madhusudana — how much less then by the Pandavas?

sanskrit: svadharmam anutiṣṭhanto yadi mādhava saṃyuge śastreṇa nidhanaṃ kāle prāpsyāmaḥ svargam eva tat
english: If, following our own duty, O Madhava, we obtain death by weapons in battle at the proper time, that is heaven itself.

sanskrit: mukhyaś caivaiṣa no dharmaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ janārdana yac chayīmahi saṃgrāme śaratalpagatā vayam
english: And this is the foremost duty of us Kshatriyas, O Janardana — that we lie in battle on a bed of arrows.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ vīraśayanaṃ prāpsyāmo yadi saṃyuge apraṇamyaiva śatrūṇāṃ na nas tapsyati mādhava
english: We shall attain the hero's death-bed in battle without ever bowing to enemies — that shall not grieve us, O Madhava.

sanskrit: kaś ca jātu kule jātaḥ kṣatradharmeṇa vartayan bhayād vṛttiṃ samīkṣyaivaṃ praṇamed iha kasya cit
english: And who, born in a noble family and living by the Kshatriya code, would ever bow here to anyone out of fear when considering his livelihood?

sanskrit: udyacched eva na named udyamo hy eva pauruṣam apy aparvaṇi bhajyeta na named iha kasya cit
english: One should only rise up, never bow down — for exertion itself is manliness; even if one breaks at an untimely moment, one should not bow to anyone here.

sanskrit: iti mātaṅgavacanaṃ parīpsanti hitepsavaḥ dharmāya caiva praṇamed brāhmaṇebhyaś ca madvidhaḥ
english: So desiring the words of the elephant-lore, those who seek their own good say: one like me bows only for righteousness and to Brahmins.

sanskrit: acintayan kaṃ cid anyaṃ yāvajjīvaṃ tathācaret eṣa dharmaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ matam etac ca me sadā
english: Without regard for anyone else, one should act so for as long as one lives — this is the duty of Kshatriyas, and this has always been my view.

sanskrit: rājyāṃśaś cābhyanujñāto yo me pitrā purābhavat na sa labhyaḥ punar jātu mayi jīvati keśava
english: And the share of the kingdom that was formerly granted to me by my father — that can never again be obtained while I live, O Keshava.

sanskrit: yāvac ca rājā dhriyate dhṛtarāṣṭro janārdana nyastaśastrā vayaṃ te vāpy upajīvāma mādhava
english: And as long as King Dhritarashtra lives, O Janardana, we shall live under him with weapons laid aside — or else serve you, O Madhava.

sanskrit: yady adeyaṃ purā dattaṃ rājyaṃ paravato mama ajñānād vā bhayād vāpi mayi bāle janārdana
english: If what was formerly given to me was the kingdom that ought not to have been given — given out of ignorance or fear, when I was a boy, O Janardana —

sanskrit: na tad adya punar labhyaṃ pāṇḍavair vṛṣṇinandana dhriyamāṇe mahābāho mayi saṃprati keśava
english: — that cannot now be gotten back by the Pandavas, O delight of the Vrishnis, O mighty-armed one, while I currently live, O Keshava.

sanskrit: yāvad dhi sūcyās tīkṣṇāyā vidhyed agreṇa mādhava tāvad apy aparityājyaṃ bhūmer naḥ pāṇḍavān prati
english: For even as much land as the tip of a sharp needle might pierce, O Madhava — that much of the earth is not to be yielded to the Pandavas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prahasya dāśārhaḥ krodhaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ duryodhanam idaṃ vākyam abravīt kurusaṃsadi
english: Vaishampayana said: Then the scion of the Dasharha clan, his eyes turbulent with anger, laughed and spoke this word to Duryodhana in the Kuru assembly.

sanskrit: lapsyase vīraśayanaṃ kāmam etad avāpsyasi sthiro bhava sahāmātyo vimardo bhavitā mahān
english: You shall obtain the hero's death-bed; you shall attain that desire of yours. Stand firm with your ministers — the great clash shall come.

sanskrit: yac caivaṃ manyase mūḍha na me kaś cid vyatikramaḥ pāṇḍaveṣv iti tat sarvaṃ nibodhata narādhipāḥ
english: And as for your thinking, O fool, 'There is no transgression of mine against the Pandavas' — hear all that, O lords of men.

sanskrit: śriyā saṃtapyamānena pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām tvayā durmantritaṃ dyūtaṃ saubalena ca bhārata
english: Burning with envy at the prosperity of the great-souled Pandavas, the dice game was wickedly devised by you and by the son of Subala, O Bharata.

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca jñātayas tāta śreyāṃsaḥ sādhusaṃmatāḥ tathānyāyyam upasthātuṃ jihmenājihmacāriṇaḥ
english: And how should kinsmen who are noble and honored by the good, themselves straightforward in conduct, lend themselves to such injustice through crooked means?

sanskrit: akṣadyūtaṃ mahāprājña satām aratināśanam asatāṃ tatra jāyante bhedāś ca vyasanāni ca
english: Dice play, O greatly wise one, destroys the happiness of the good; among the wicked it generates schisms and calamities.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ vyasanaṃ ghoraṃ tvayā dyūtamukhaṃ kṛtam asamīkṣya sadācāraiḥ sārdhaṃ pāpānubandhanaiḥ
english: This dreadful calamity was brought about by you through the dice game, without consulting those of good conduct, together with associates given to sin.

sanskrit: kaś cānyo jñātibhāryāṃ vai viprakartuṃ tathārhati ānīya ca sabhāṃ vaktuṃ yathoktā draupadī tvayā
english: And who else among kinsmen deserves to dishonor a kinsman's wife in such a way — to drag her into the assembly and speak of her as Draupadi was spoken of by you?

sanskrit: kulīnā śīlasaṃpannā prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasī mahiṣī pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ tathā vinikṛtā tvayā
english: Noble-born and endowed with virtue, dearer than life itself — the queen of the sons of Pandu was dishonored by you in that manner.

sanskrit: jānanti kuravaḥ sarve yathoktāḥ kurusaṃsadi duḥśāsanena kaunteyāḥ pravrajantaḥ paraṃtapāḥ
english: All the Kurus know how the sons of Kunti, those scorchers of foes, were addressed in the Kuru assembly by Duhshasana as they set out for the forest.

sanskrit: samyagvṛtteṣv alubdheṣu satataṃ dharmacāriṣu sveṣu bandhuṣu kaḥ sādhuś cared evam asāṃpratam
english: Who that is good would act so improperly toward kinsmen of his own who behave correctly, who are free from greed, and who constantly walk in righteousness?

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsānām anāryāṇāṃ paruṣāṇāṃ ca bhāṣaṇam karṇaduḥśāsanābhyāṃ ca tvayā ca bahuśaḥ kṛtam
english: Cruel, ignoble, and harsh words were spoken many times by Karna and Duhshasana and by you yourself.

sanskrit: saha mātrā pradagdhuṃ tān bālakān vāraṇāvate āsthitaḥ paramaṃ yatnaṃ na samṛddhaṃ ca tat tava
english: At Varanavata you made the utmost effort to burn those children together with their mother — yet that did not succeed for you.

sanskrit: ūṣuś ca suciraṃ kālaṃ pracchannāḥ pāṇḍavās tadā mātrā sahaikacakrāyāṃ brāhmaṇasya niveśane
english: And then the Pandavas lived hidden for a long time together with their mother in the house of a Brahmin in the city of Ekachakra.

sanskrit: viṣeṇa sarpabandhaiś ca yatitāḥ pāṇḍavās tvayā sarvopāyair vināśāya na samṛddhaṃ ca tat tava
english: The Pandavas were attacked by you with poison and with the bonds of serpents, and with every means of destruction — yet that too did not succeed for you.

sanskrit: evaṃbuddhiḥ pāṇḍaveṣu mithyāvṛttiḥ sadā bhavān kathaṃ te nāparādho 'sti pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu
english: Such is your intent toward the Pandavas, and your conduct toward them has always been deceitful — how then is there no offense of yours against the great-souled Pandavas?

sanskrit: kṛtvā bahūny akāryāṇi pāṇḍaveṣu nṛśaṃsavat mithyāvṛttir anāryaḥ sann adya vipratipadyase
english: Having done many wicked deeds toward the Pandavas in a cruel manner, being of false conduct and ignoble, you now contradict yourself.

sanskrit: mātāpitṛbhyāṃ bhīṣmeṇa droṇena vidureṇa ca śāmyeti muhur ukto 'si na ca śāmyasi pārthiva
english: By your mother and father, by Bhishma, by Drona, and by Vidura you have been told again and again to make peace — yet you do not make peace, O king.

sanskrit: śame hi sumahān arthas tava pārthasya cobhayoḥ na ca rocayase rājan kim anyad buddhilāghavāt
english: For in peace there is a very great benefit for you and for Partha both — yet you do not find it pleasing, O king. What else can it be but lightness of intellect?

sanskrit: na śarma prāpsyase rājann utkramya suhṛdāṃ vacaḥ adharmyam ayaśasyaṃ ca kriyate pārthiva tvayā
english: You shall not attain happiness, O king, by transgressing the words of your well-wishers; what you do, O king, is both unrighteous and ignoble.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati dāśārhe duryodhanam amarṣaṇam duḥśāsana idaṃ vākyam abravīt kurusaṃsadi
english: While the scion of the Dasharha clan was speaking thus to the wrathful Duryodhana, Duhshasana spoke this word in the Kuru assembly.

sanskrit: na cet saṃdhāsyase rājan svena kāmena pāṇḍavaiḥ baddhvā kila tvāṃ dāsyanti kuntīputrāya kauravāḥ
english: If you do not make peace with the Pandavas of your own free will, O king, they say the Kauravas will bind you and hand you over to the son of Kunti.

sanskrit: vaikartanaṃ tvāṃ ca māṃ ca trīn etān manujarṣabha pāṇḍavebhyaḥ pradāsyanti bhīṣmo droṇaḥ pitā ca te
english: Bhishma, Drona, and your own father shall hand over these three — you, me, and the son of Vikartana — to the Pandavas, O bull among men.

sanskrit: bhrātur etad vacaḥ śrutvā dhārtarāṣṭraḥ suyodhanaḥ kruddhaḥ prātiṣṭhatotthāya mahānāga iva śvasan
english: Having heard this speech of his brother, Suyodhana the son of Dhritarashtra rose up in fury and strode away, hissing like a great serpent.
